title: Task-Dependent Linguistic Measures in Aphasia Discourse: A Comparative Analysis of Narrative, Descriptive, and Procedural Speech
abstract: arXiv:2611.30826v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Background: Transcript-based measures such as word counts, lexical diversity and disfluency rates are widely used to describe language ability in aphasia. Each measure comes from a specific elicitation task, and studies use different tasks, so values from different tasks may not be comparable. Aims: To test whether discourse tasks change these measures within the same speakers, and whether the measures follow a gradient from Procedural to Descriptive to Narrative discourse. Methods & Procedures: Baseline transcripts from 61 adults with chronic post-stroke aphasia were taken from the Fridriksson-2 corpus in AphasiaBank (POLAR trial, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03416738). Each speaker produced a Procedural (Sandwich), a Descriptive (Broken Window) and a Narrative (Cinderella) sample in one session. A rule-based pipeline extracted 13 measures, 10 of which were common enough to test. Friedman, Page and Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate corr

translated_title: 失语症话语中任务依赖的语言学测量指标：叙事性、描述性与程序性言语的比较分析
translated_abstract: 背景：基于转录文本的测量指标（如词数、词汇多样性和不流畅率）被广泛用于描述失语症患者的语言能力。每项指标均来自特定的言语引导任务，而不同研究使用不同的任务，因此来自不同任务的数值可能并不具有可比性。研究目的：检验话语任务是否会改变同一说话者的这些测量指标，以及这些指标是否遵循从程序性、描述性到叙事性话语的梯度变化规律。方法与步骤：61名慢性卒中后失语症成年患者的基线转录文本取自AphasiaBank的Fridriksson-2语料库（POLAR试验，ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03416738）。每位说话者在同一次会话中分别完成一项程序性任务（制作三明治）、一项描述性任务（破窗户图片描述）和一项叙事性任务（灰姑娘故事讲述）。基于规则的流水线提取了13项指标，其中10项指标因出现频率足够高而可用于统计检验。采用Friedman检验、Page趋势检验和Wilcoxon检验，并进行错误发现率校正（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究通过对61名慢性卒中后失语症患者在同一会话中完成的三种话语任务（程序性、描述性、叙事性）进行10项语言学测量指标的比较分析，证明话语任务类型本身会显著影响失语症的转录文本测量结果，因此不同任务得到的数值不能直接混用比较。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates through comparative analysis of three discourse tasks (procedural, descriptive, and narrative) in 61 adults with chronic post-stroke aphasia that transcript-based linguistic measures are task-dependent and thus values obtained from different elicitation tasks may not be directly comparable.
